ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
As shown in the figure, a child with a mass of $30\mathrm{kg}$ is sitting on a sled with a mass of $10\mathrm{kg}$. An adult pulls the sled with a force of $100N$ at an angle of $37^{\circ}$ above the horizontal, causing the sled to move at a constant speed along the horizontal ground. Given that $\sin37^{\circ}{=}0.6$, $\cos37^{\circ}=0.8$, and taking $g{=}10\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$, find:

1. What is the magnitude of the pressure exerted by the sled on the ground?
2. What is the magnitude of the kinetic friction coefficient between the sled and the horizontal ground?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure is a child sitting on a sled, and the sled is on horizontal ground; on the right side an adult pulls the sled obliquely upward through a rope. The pulling force on the rope is labeled F, and its direction makes an angle θ with the horizontal dashed line, indicating that the pulling force has a horizontal rightward component and a vertical upward component. Reasoning: According to the meaning of the problem and the draft method, regard the child and the sled as one whole. The total mass is 30 kg + 10 kg = 40 kg, so the total gravity is mg = 40 × 10 = 400 N, directed vertically downward. The pulling force F = 100 N, the included angle is 37°, and its vertical component is F_y = 100 sin37° = 100 × 0.6 = 60 N, directed upward; the horizontal component is F_x = 100 cos37° = 100 × 0.8 = 80 N, directed to the right. Since the sled moves at constant speed along horizontal ground, the resultant force in the vertical direction is zero, so N + F_y = mg, giving N = 400 - 60 = 340 N. The magnitude of the supporting force of the ground on the sled is 340 N, and from action and reaction it can be known that the magnitude of the pressure of the sled on the ground is also 340 N. The resultant force in the horizontal direction is also zero, so the kinetic friction force f_k = F_x = 80 N. From f_k = μ_k N, μ_k = 80 / 340 ≈ 0.235, about 0.24.
